correctness.rationale: Any real signal decomposes into signed steps with coefficient l1 sum equal TV; stochastic symmetry identifies the step L1 error as twice the heat mass crossing a cut. Edge/vertex intertwining gives E_k prime=2(exp(-tDD^T))_{kk}. The Dirichlet edge matrix has the stated sine spectrum. Odd reflection into the 2N-cycle, followed by strict radial monotonicity of cycle heat proven via an irreducible cooperative first-difference ODE, establishes the strictly centralized maxima at every t>0. For any two nonzero jumps the signed output errors necessarily disagree at a vertex, excluding multiple-jump equality. Spectral positivity gives strict temporal concavity and the stationary-law limit; summable 1/r^2 domination proves the diffusive scaling. Packaged standalone NumPy/SciPy checker passed 11,325 finite matrix/spectral/BV inequalities and 170 exact integer adjacency bridge checks; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Finite reflecting path heat is a basic stable diffusion discretization. Exact BV-to-counting-L1 error at every grid size and time is a useful discrete calibration for jump-containing data, and central-cut rigidity distinguishes the worst discontinuity from arbitrary-location rate bounds. Strict temporal concavity and explicit diffusive bridging explain how finite-grid and continuum approximation error regimes relate. The value is the all-N/t sharp norm with equality classification, not a routine restatement of the sine spectrum or an arbitrary small numerical improvement.
